title: Check your understanding: Rebasing onto a Selected Base

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of rebasing onto a selected base?
options: `git rebase --onto` selects a new base and a commit range to replay. Verify the old base, target base and branch before running because an incorrect range can move unrelated changes.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: `git rebase --onto` selects a new base and a commit range to replay. Verify the old base, target base and branch before running because an incorrect range can move unrelated changes.
questions.explanation: `git rebase --onto` selects a new base and a commit range to replay. Verify the old base, target base and branch before running because an incorrect range can move unrelated changes.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git rebase --onto new-base old-base feature/example` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with rebasing onto a selected base?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
